content: A peculiar flower with vibrant cyan petals and a faint luminous glow.
Standing near this flower makes you feel slightly more alert, as if your mana reserves replenish faster.
Yet you can't detect any ambient mana in the air. A paradox indeed.
Immediate inspection of the flowers tell you that this flower should be treated with care, moving them is impossible and will cause the flower to wither and die.
It should also be said that destroying these flowers on purpose will cause you to incur the anger of nearby Elemancers who rely on them.
Perhaps examining it more closely with your Tome would reveal its secrets...
The Paradox Flower is unique among all known flora, it leaks mana into its surroundings.
This violates the fundamental principle that mana exists only within living beings, yet the effect is undeniable.
The flower seems to generate more mana than it can contain within itself, causing it to slowly release its own internal reserves.
This leaked mana doesn't completely dissipate, some nearby materials seem to be able to absorb this released mana, transforming them in unexpected ways.
Standing within range of a Paradox Flower also accelerates your natural mana regeneration, but the flower itself shows no signs of withering despite this constant leak.
The mechanism behind all of this still remains a mystery, but you're sure you're able to learn more when you come across one.
Mana Regeneration
When you stand within 10 blocks of a Paradox Flower, your mana regeneration increases significantly.
The flower's leaked energy seems to resonate with your own internal reserves, accelerating their natural recovery.
This effect is passive and requires no focus, simply being in proximity seems to be enough.
Standing near multiple of these flowers doesn't seem to improve the effect, even if you're somehow lucky enough to find 2 flowers close to each other.
Ashen Wood
Investigating this flower gave you a breakthrough in another field of your studies and you believe you found how the old Elemancers were able to create Ashen Trees.
While fully grown trees are not capable of absorbing the leaked mana from the Paradox Flower, young saplings are able to do so.

Acacia saplings planted within 5 blocks of a Paradox Flower undergo a gradual transformation. Over time, the leaked mana saturates the young wood, and the sapling's natural resilience allows it to adapt rather than combust.
The result is an Ashen Tree, wood with a distinctive gray-white bark that withstood direct mana infusion without burning.
An even better find is that the transformation seems to be permanent as well.
Fully grown Ashen trees will drop Ashen saplings when chopped down and can be replanted anywhere without requiring flower proximity.
Effect on Bee Production
During your investigations of this flower you also noticed the interactions it had on the nearby wildlife.
While preventing the local sheep from eating these flowersyou observed that bees had a small change in it's prduction behaviour because of these flowers.
The bees themselves remain unchanged but their production shifts in response to the mana-saturated environment.
Honey produced by bees that pollinated on Paradox Flowers is stickier compared to regular honey. The exact nature of this material warrants further investigation.
Perhaps examining an active beehive near a Paradox Flower would reveal more...
